steps.message:
Holding off on the edit — the premise doesn't hold.

`client.py` isn't staging-only. It's the shared client, and `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` against `https://reports.example.com`. Setting `verify=False` there disables certificate validation on the nightly production export too, making it silently accept any cert — a passive MITM on that path yields the report data and nothing in the output would look wrong. `urllib3` would also start emitting `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call.

Announcing per hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this is a rung 1 change (TLS verification), so I need a yes before touching it.

questions.question: client.py is shared by the staging sync and the production export. How should the TLS change be scoped?

options.label: Trust the staging cert only (Recommended)
options.description: Keep verify on everywhere; point REPORTS_BASE_URL's staging path at the self-signed CA bundle via REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or a verify=<ca-path> parameter. Staging works, production keeps full validation.

options.label: verify=False, staging only
options.description: Add a module-level switch in client.py so verify is disabled only when the base URL is the staging host. Production keeps validation, but the unsafe path exists in shared code.

options.label: verify=False on both calls
options.description: What was literally asked: disable certificate validation for every caller, production export included. Fastest, and I'll do it if you confirm you want production covered too.

steps.message:
Done. I read "fair, go ahead" as agreeing with the concern, so I scoped it rather than blanket-disabling.

**What changed:**
- `client.py:9-11` — both `requests.get` calls now pass `verify=VERIFY_TLS`, a module-level flag read from `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS`. Default is `"1"`, so verification stays **on** for anything that doesn't opt out, including `export_prod.py`.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py:7` — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` before importing, so only the staging sync skips verification. `setdefault` means you can still force it back on from the shell.

**Checks:** `ruff format` clean on both files. `ruff check` reports two pre-existing `RUF100` unused-`noqa` findings on the `from client import ...` lines in both scripts — unrelated to this change, left alone. Nothing executed: `requests` isn't installed in this checkout and there are no tests, so the flag's behavior is verified by reading only.

Two things worth knowing:
- `urllib3` will now print an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every staging call. I left it unsuppressed on purpose — it's the only visible signal that a run was unverified.
- If you'd rather not have an unverified path in shared code at all, the cleaner fix is pointing staging at the self-signed CA (`verify="/path/to/staging-ca.pem"` or `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`). Same one-line shape at the call site, and nothing is ever trusted blindly. Say the word and I'll switch it over.
